References / Editorial / 538

Smashing Magazine, “The Split Personality of Brutalist Web Development”

An essay that splits web brutalism into l’Internet brut, built from raw HTML, and l’Internet fou, built for shock.

Source
Smashing Magazine
Creator
Frederick O’Brien
Made

Style
Brutalist web design (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)

Evidence
Article text read on 2026-10-02. The publication time (8 January 2020) is in the page’s metadata, and the author link is on the page. The article’s screenshots were not inspected.

Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

“Type One: l’Internet Brut … where the raw materials are HTML and, to a lesser extent, CSS. The backgrounds are light, the text is black, and the hyperlinks are blue.”

Examples it names for the raw type: the first website, David Bryant Copeland’s Brutalist Web Design, Craigslist, Wikipedia, the old A List Apart, old Reddit, Bloomberg, and Freecycle.

“Type Two: l’Internet Fou” covers the many “brutalist” sites built to provoke. It quotes Vitaly Friedman: brutalism in architecture is “unconcerned aesthetics, not intentionally broken aesthetics”.

Why it belongs

Its Type One is the scope of Brutalist web design. Some of its examples, such as Bloomberg, are bolder than default HTML and need a capture before they count as evidence.

Borrow

Treat HTML as the material: let the structure of the document set the look, and shape each page around its content.
